title: Dynamic Attribution of Hematologic Worsening Following ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 Therapy in Patients with Bone-Metastatic mCRPC: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study
summary: This study investigates why blood counts worsen during ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 therapy in patients with advanced prostate cancer. The aim is to distinguish whether these changes are mainly caused by disease progression or by treatment, thereby improving patient management and treatment decisions.

interventions.name: This is a multicenter retrospective observational cohort study. Clinical, laboratory, treatment, and imaging data will be collected from participating centers. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma.
Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) with bone metastases.
Treatment with at least two cycles of 177Lu-PSMA-617 therapy.
Availability of baseline clinical and laboratory data before treatment.
At least one follow-up laboratory assessment after treatment.
Sufficient clinical documentation for retrospective analysis.
Exclusion criteria:
Fewer than two treatment cycles.
Missing key baseline or follow-up laboratory data.
Follow-up insufficient for hematologic status assessment.
Patients receiving concomitant treatments that independently caused severe hematologic toxicity (when identifiable).
